newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAKIA TO CUT 1997 GRAIN CROP ESTIMATE - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAKIA TO CUT 1997 GRAIN CROP ESTIMATE - PAPER.

text.p: Slovakia's 1997 grain harvest will be lower than original estimates due to more than a week of constant rainfall causing damage to crops and property, the economic daily Hospodarske Noviny said on Tuesday.
Quoting Agriculture Minister Peter Baco, the paper said that about one third of the grain crop had been flattened by the rain and would be difficult to harvest.
Ministry officicals were not immediately available for additional comment.
"Exact information (on the extent of the damage) and and damage estimates will only be availabe in a few days time," the daily said.
Last week the Slovak Statistical Bureau (SUSR) estimated the 1997 grain harvest to yield up to 3.12 million tonnes, an increase of 19.1 percent over 1996.
The rapeseed harvest has been estimated at between 199,000 and 208,000 tonnes, an increase of 42.6 percent over 1996, SUSR said last week.
Rain and floods have delayed the harvest in southern Slovakia, the country's granary, the official news agency TASR reported quoting regional agricultural authorities.
The only some 1,500 hectares, or 0.81 percent out of total 190,017 hectares of sown grain has so far been harvested in the southern region, the agency said.
In addition to a delay in the harvest the floods have also resulted in under-average grain yields, TASR said.
According to premilinary figures the yield of the winter wheat will decrease to 4.42 tonnes per hectare from an earlier estimate of 4.9 tonnes per hectare.

The winter barley yield however is expected to increase to 4.42 tonnes per hectare from the original estimate of 4.28 tonnes per hectare, the agency added. -- Peter Javurek, Bratislava Newsroom, 421-7-521 8402
